88	    def add(self, relative_path, tags=()):
89	        path = (self.root / relative_path).resolve()
90	        if not path.is_relative_to(self.root) or not path.is_file():
91	            raise ValueError("document must be a file inside the document root")
92	        clean_tags = sorted({tag.strip().lower() for tag in tags if tag.strip()})
93	        key = path.relative_to(self.root).as_posix()
94	        content = path.read_bytes()
95	        record = {"path": key, "name": path.name, "bytes": len(content),
96	                  "sha256": hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest(), "tags": clean_tags}
97	        records = self._load()
98	        existing = records.get(key)
99	        if isinstance(existing, dict) and "references" in existing:
100	            record["references"] = existing["references"]
101	        if isinstance(existing, dict) and "archived" in existing:
102	            record["archived"] = existing["archived"]
103	        if isinstance(existing, dict) and "category" in existing:
104	            record["category"] = existing["category"]
105	        if isinstance(existing, dict) and "version_note" in existing:
106	            record["version_note"] = existing["version_note"]
107	        records[key] = record
108	        self.index.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
109	        self.index.write_text(json.dumps(records, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
110	        return record
111	
112	    def set_references(self, relative_path, targets):
113	        if not isinstance(relative_path, str):
114	            raise ValueError("source path must be a string")
115	        if (not isinstance(targets, list)
116	                or not all(isinstance(target, str) for target in targets)):
117	            raise ValueError("targets must be a list of strings")
118	        records = self._load_validated_with_references()
119	        if relative_path not in records:
120	            raise ValueError("source document is not registered")
121	        for target in targets:
122	            if target not in records:
123	                raise ValueError("reference target is not registered")
124	        record = records[relative_path]
125	        record["references"] = sorted(set(targets))
126	        self.index.write_text(json.dumps(records, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
127	        return record
128	
129	    def set_archived(self, relative_path, archived):
130	        if not isinstance(relative_path, str):
131	            raise ValueError("document path must be a string")
132	        if not isinstance(archived, bool):
133	            raise ValueError("archived must be a boolean")
134	        records = self._load_validated_with_references()
135	        if relative_path not in records:
136	            raise ValueError("document is not registered")
137	        record = records[relative_path]
138	        record["archived"] = archived
139	        self.index.write_text(json.dumps(records, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
140	        return record
141	
142	    def set_category(self, relative_path, category):
143	        if not isinstance(relative_path, str):
144	            raise ValueError("document path must be a string")
145	        if not isinstance(category, str):
146	            raise ValueError("category must be a string")
147	        records = self._load_validated_with_categories()
148	        if relative_path not in records:
149	            raise ValueError("document is not registered")
150	        record = records[relative_path]
151	        record["category"] = category.strip()
152	        self.index.write_text(json.dumps(records, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
153	        return record
154	
155	    def set_version_note(self, relative_path, note):
156	        if not isinstance(relative_path, str):
157	            raise ValueError("document path must be a string")
158	        if not isinstance(note, str):
159	            raise ValueError("version note must be a string")
160	        records = self._load_validated_with_version_notes()
161	        if relative_path not in records:
162	            raise ValueError("document is not registered")
163	        record = records[relative_path]
164	        record["version_note"] = note.strip()
165	        self.index.write_text(json.dumps(records, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
166	        return record
167	
168	    @staticmethod
169	    def _normalize_tags(tags):
170	        return {tag.strip().lower() for tag in tags if tag.strip()}
171	
172	    def edit_tags(self, paths, add_tags=(), remove_tags=()):
173	        if not isinstance(paths, (list, tuple)):
174	            raise ValueError("paths must be a list or tuple of strings")
175	        if not isinstance(add_tags, (list, tuple)):
176	            raise ValueError("add_tags must be a list or tuple of strings")
177	        if not isinstance(remove_tags, (list, tuple)):
178	            raise ValueError("remove_tags must be a list or tuple of strings")
179	        if (not all(isinstance(path, str) for path in paths)
180	                or not all(isinstance(tag, str) for tag in add_tags)
181	                or not all(isinstance(tag, str) for tag in remove_tags)):
182	            raise ValueError("paths and tags must contain only strings")
183	        # The whole index must be structurally sound before anything changes.
184	        records = self._load_validated_with_version_notes()
185	        unique_paths = list(dict.fromkeys(paths))  # duplicates handled once, first occurrence wins
186	        for path in unique_paths:
187	            if path not in records:
188	                raise ValueError("document is not registered: " + path)
189	        added = self._normalize_tags(add_tags)
190	        removed = self._normalize_tags(remove_tags)
191	        if added & removed:
192	            raise ValueError("add_tags and remove_tags overlap after normalization")
193	        updated = []
194	        unchanged = []
195	        for path in sorted(unique_paths):
196	            record = records[path]
197	            new_tags = sorted((self._normalize_tags(record["tags"]) - removed) | added)
198	            if new_tags == record["tags"]:
199	                unchanged.append(path)
200	            else:  # only the tags array changes; every other field stays as stored
201	                record["tags"] = new_tags
202	                updated.append(record)
203	        if updated:
204	            self.index.write_text(json.dumps(records, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n",
205	                                  encoding="utf-8")
206	        return {"updated": updated,
207	                "unchanged": unchanged}
208	
209	    def remove_record(self, relative_path, detach=False):
210	        if not isinstance(relative_path, str):
211	            raise ValueError("document path must be a string")
212	        if not isinstance(detach, bool):
213	            raise ValueError("detach must be a boolean")
214	        records = self._load_validated_with_categories()
215	        if relative_path not in records:
216	            raise ValueError("document is not registered")
217	        removed = records[relative_path]
218	        updated = []
219	        for source, record in records.items():
220	            if source == relative_path or "references" not in record:
221	                continue
222	            remaining = [target for target in record["references"]
223	                         if target != relative_path]
224	            # The target's own references never block its removal.
225	            if len(remaining) != len(record["references"]):
226	                if not detach:
227	                    raise ValueError("document is referenced by another record")
228	                record["references"] = remaining
229	                updated.append(record)
230	        del records[relative_path]
231	        self.index.write_text(json.dumps(records, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
232	        return {"removed": removed,
233	                "updated": sorted(updated, key=lambda record: record["path"])}
234	
235	    def relocate_record(self, source, destination):
236	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not isinstance(destination, str):
237	            raise ValueError("source and destination paths must be strings")
238	        # The whole index must be structurally sound before anything changes.
239	        records = self._load_validated_with_version_notes()
240	        if source not in records:
241	            raise ValueError("source document is not registered")
242	        # The destination is resolved against the live filesystem exactly like
243	        # add; the source key is never resolved or read.
244	        try:
245	            path = (self.root / destination).resolve()
246	        except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError):
247	            raise ValueError("destination must be a file inside the document root")
248	        if not path.is_relative_to(self.root):
249	            raise ValueError("destination must be a file inside the document root")
250	        if not path.is_file():
251	            raise ValueError("destination must be a file inside the document root")
252	        key = path.relative_to(self.root).as_posix()
253	        if key in records:  # the destination key must be free, source itself included
254	            raise ValueError("destination document is already registered")
255	        original = records[source]
256	        content = path.read_bytes()
257	        if (len(content) != original["bytes"]
258	                or hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest() != original["sha256"]):
259	            raise ValueError("destination content does not match the registered bytes or sha256")
260	        before = dict(original)
261	        after = dict(original)
262	        after["path"] = key
263	        after["name"] = path.name
264	        if "references" in after:  # the moved record's own self-reference follows too
265	            after["references"] = [key if target == source else target
266	                                   for target in after["references"]]
267	        # Every other record's references to the old key follow it to the new
268	        # key; order and duplicates are preserved and records without references
269	        # stay untouched.
270	        updated = []
271	        for other, record in records.items():
272	            if other == source or "references" not in record:
273	                continue
274	            if source in record["references"]:
275	                record["references"] = [key if target == source else target
276	                                        for target in record["references"]]
277	                updated.append(record)
278	        del records[source]
279	        records[key] = after
280	        self.index.write_text(json.dumps(records, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n",
281	                              encoding="utf-8")
282	        return {"before": before,
283	                "after": after,
284	                "updated": sorted(updated, key=lambda record: record["path"])}

286	    @staticmethod
287	    def _validate_importable(records):
288	        # Per-record field and type checks shared by the stored index and an
289	        # import batch; reference targets are resolved separately, against the
290	        # merged index.
291	        for key, record in records.items():
292	            if (not isinstance(key, str) or not isinstance(record, dict)
293	                    or record.get("path") != key):
294	                raise ValueError("records must be objects keyed by their path")
295	            if (not isinstance(record.get("name"), str)
296	                    or not isinstance(record.get("bytes"), int)
297	                    or isinstance(record.get("bytes"), bool)
298	                    or not isinstance(record.get("sha256"), str)
299	                    or not isinstance(record.get("tags"), list)
300	                    or not all(isinstance(tag, str) for tag in record["tags"])):
301	                raise ValueError("record has invalid field types")
302	            if "archived" in record and not isinstance(record["archived"], bool):
303	                raise ValueError("record archived must be a boolean")
304	            references = record.get("references", [])
305	            if (not isinstance(references, list)
306	                    or not all(isinstance(target, str) for target in references)):
307	                raise ValueError("record references must be a list of strings")
308	            if "category" in record and not isinstance(record["category"], str):
309	                raise ValueError("record category must be a string")

311	    def import_records(self, batch):
312	        if not isinstance(batch, dict):
313	            raise ValueError("import batch must be an object of records")
314	        existing = self._load()
315	        if not isinstance(existing, dict):
316	            raise ValueError("index must be a JSON object of records")
317	        # Bad records fail the whole batch even when their paths are not imported.
318	        self._validate_importable(existing)
319	        self._validate_importable(batch)
320	        added = []
321	        unchanged = []
322	        for key, record in batch.items():
323	            if key not in existing:
324	                added.append(key)
325	            elif existing[key] == record:  # field set and values, arrays ordered
326	                unchanged.append(key)
327	            else:
328	                raise ValueError("import conflicts with the existing record: " + key)
329	        merged = dict(existing)
330	        for key in added:
331	            merged[key] = batch[key]
332	        for record in merged.values():
333	            for target in record.get("references", []):
334	                if target not in merged:
335	                    raise ValueError("record references an unregistered path")
336	        if added:
337	            self.index.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
338	            self.index.write_text(json.dumps(merged, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n",
339	                                  encoding="utf-8")
340	        return {"added": sorted(added), "unchanged": sorted(unchanged)}

342	    def export_records(self, tags=(), text="", archive_state="all", category=None):
343	        if not isinstance(tags, (list, tuple)) or not all(isinstance(tag, str) for tag in tags):
344	            raise ValueError("tags must be a list or tuple of strings")
345	        if not isinstance(text, str):
346	            raise ValueError("text must be a string")
347	        self._check_archive_state(archive_state)
348	        self._check_category_filter(category)
349	        records = self._load_validated_with_categories()
350	        wanted = {tag.strip().lower() for tag in tags if tag.strip()}
351	
352	        def matches(record):
353	            return (wanted.issubset(record["tags"])
354	                    and text.casefold() in record["path"].casefold()
355	                    and self._matches_archive_state(record, archive_state)
356	                    and self._matches_category(record, category))
357	
358	        selected = {}
359	        stack = [key for key, record in records.items() if matches(record)]
360	        while stack:
361	            key = stack.pop()
362	            if key in selected:
363	                continue
364	            selected[key] = records[key]
365	            # Dependencies are pulled in regardless of the filters; records
366	            # that merely reference a selected one are not.
367	            stack.extend(records[key].get("references", []))
368	        return {key: selected[key] for key in sorted(selected)}

370	    def reference_impact(self, target, transitive=False, include_routes=False):
371	        if not isinstance(target, str):
372	            raise ValueError("target path must be a string")
373	        if not isinstance(transitive, bool):
374	            raise ValueError("transitive must be a boolean")
375	        if not isinstance(include_routes, bool):
376	            raise ValueError("include_routes must be a boolean")
377	        records = self._load_validated_with_references()
378	        if target not in records:
379	            raise ValueError("target document is not registered")
380	        referrers = {}
381	        for source, record in records.items():
382	            for referenced in record.get("references", []):
383	                referrers.setdefault(referenced, set()).add(source)
384	        distances = {}
385	        frontier = [target]
386	        depth = 0
387	        while frontier and (transitive or depth == 0):
388	            nxt = []
389	            for node in frontier:
390	                for source in referrers.get(node, ()):  # reverse reference edges
391	                    if source != target and source not in distances:
392	                        distances[source] = depth + 1
393	                        nxt.append(source)
394	            frontier = nxt
395	            depth += 1
396	        routes = {}
397	        if include_routes:
398	            # One shortest chain per referrer, from the referrer to the target.
399	            # Built level by level so every next hop's best suffix is already
400	            # known; equal-length chains tie-break on the case-sensitive
401	            # lexicographic order of the full path array.
402	            for key in sorted(distances, key=lambda key: (distances[key], key)):
403	                suffixes = []
404	                for referenced in records[key].get("references", []):
405	                    if referenced == target and distances[key] == 1:
406	                        suffixes.append([target])
407	                    elif (referenced in distances
408	                          and distances[referenced] == distances[key] - 1):
409	                        suffixes.append(routes[referenced])
410	                routes[key] = [key] + min(suffixes)
411	        documents = []
412	        for key in sorted(distances, key=lambda key: (distances[key], key)):
413	            document = {**records[key], "distance": distances[key]}
414	            if include_routes:
415	                document["route"] = routes[key]
416	            documents.append(document)
417	        return {"path": target, "documents": documents}
418	
419	    def search(self, tags=(), text="", archive_state="all", category=None):
420	        self._check_archive_state(archive_state)
421	        self._check_category_filter(category)
422	        wanted = {tag.strip().lower() for tag in tags if tag.strip()}
423	        if archive_state == "all" and category is None:
424	            records = self._load()
425	        else:  # a non-trivial filter validates the whole index, references included
426	            records = self._load_validated_with_categories()
427	        return [record for _, record in sorted(records.items())
428	                if wanted.issubset(record["tags"])
429	                and text.casefold() in record["path"].casefold()
430	                and self._matches_archive_state(record, archive_state)
431	                and self._matches_category(record, category)]
432	
433	    def find_duplicates(self, tags=(), text=""):
434	        if not isinstance(tags, (list, tuple)) or not all(isinstance(tag, str) for tag in tags):
435	            raise ValueError("tags must be a list or tuple of strings")
436	        if not isinstance(text, str):
437	            raise ValueError("text must be a string")
438	        records = self._load_validated_with_references()
439	        wanted = {tag.strip().lower() for tag in tags if tag.strip()}
440	
441	        def matches(record):
442	            return (wanted.issubset(record["tags"])
443	                    and text.casefold() in record["path"].casefold())
444	
445	        buckets = {}
446	        for record in records.values():
447	            buckets.setdefault((record["bytes"], record["sha256"]), []).append(record)
448	        groups = []
449	        for (size, digest), members in buckets.items():
450	            if len(members) < 2:  # duplicates need at least two distinct paths
451	                continue
452	            paths = sorted(record["path"] for record in members)
453	            matched = [path for path in paths if matches(records[path])]
454	            if not matched:  # a filter must hit at least one member to return the group
455	                continue
456	            groups.append({"bytes": size, "sha256": digest, "matched": matched,
457	                           "documents": [records[path] for path in paths]})
458	        groups.sort(key=lambda group: group["documents"][0]["path"])
459	        return {"groups": groups}

464	            if not path.is_relative_to(self.root):
465	                return "unsafe"
466	            if not path.is_file():
467	                return "missing"

470	                    and hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest() == record["sha256"]

475	    def export_manifest(self, release, tags=(), text="", include_references=False,
476	                        archive_state="all", category=None, include_origins=False,
477	                        include_version_notes=False):
478	        if not isinstance(release, str) or not release.strip():
479	            raise ValueError("release must be a non-empty string")
480	        self._check_archive_state(archive_state)
481	        self._check_category_filter(category)

483	            raise ValueError("include_origins must be a boolean")
484	        if include_origins and not include_references:

486	        if not isinstance(include_version_notes, bool):

490	
491	        def matches(record):
492	            return (wanted.issubset(record["tags"])
493	                    and text.casefold() in record["path"].casefold()
494	                    and self._matches_archive_state(record, archive_state)
495	                    and self._matches_category(record, category))
496	
497	        if include_version_notes:
498	            records = self._load_validated_with_version_notes()
499	        elif include_references or archive_state != "all" or category is not None:
500	            records = self._load_validated_with_categories()
501	        else:
502	            records = self._load_validated()
503	        if include_references:
504	            selected = {}
505	            starts = [key for key, record in records.items() if matches(record)]
506	            stack = list(starts)
507	            while stack:
508	                key = stack.pop()
509	                if key in selected:
510	                    continue
511	                selected[key] = records[key]
512	                # Referenced documents are pulled in regardless of archive state
513	                # or category.
514	                stack.extend(records[key].get("references", []))
515	            ordered = [selected[key] for key in sorted(selected)]
516	            origins = {}
517	            if include_origins:

519	                # direction; every reachable document keeps the shortest distance

523	                    frontier = [start]

1	# Document Room
2	
3	A local file metadata index. Python 3.10+ and the standard library are sufficient.
4	
5	Run `python3 document_room.py add policy.md --tag legal --tag policy` from this directory to index the sample policy. Add the second sample with `python3 document_room.py add meeting.txt --tag operations`. `python3 document_room.py search --tag legal --text policy` returns matching metadata as JSON. Multiple tags are combined with AND; tags are trimmed and lowercase, and text matches the relative path without case sensitivity.
6	
7	The default document root is `samples`; metadata is persisted in `.state/documents.json`. Override these with `--root` and `--index` before the subcommand. Re-adding a file refreshes its size, SHA-256 and tags. Search reads the stored metadata, not live file contents. Files must resolve inside the document root. This version does not copy documents, extract content or watch filesystem changes. Use the Python `DocumentRoom.add` and `DocumentRoom.search` methods for the same operations. CLI errors return JSON and exit 2.
8	
9	## Document archiving
10	
11	`python3 document_room.py archive meeting.txt` flips a registered document into the archived state without touching its file, and `DocumentRoom.set_archived(relative_path, archived)` does the same from Python; pass `--restore` (or `archived=False`) to mark it active again. The positional path matches the index's relative-path key exactly and case-sensitively, exactly as for `refs`: it is never resolved against the filesystem, the file is not parsed, and archiving or restoring works even when the original file has been deleted. The state is stored as a boolean `archived` field on the record; records written before this feature simply lack the field and are treated as active, without the field being added. Restoring stores `archived: false` explicitly. Setting the same state twice returns the identical record, and no other metadata or references change. The updated full record is printed as JSON with exit 0.
12	
13	The first `add` of a path never stores an `archived` field; re-adding a path that already has the field keeps its archived state along with its references. `search` and `export` (CLI flag `--archive-state`, Python argument `archive_state`) accept only `all`, `active` and `archived`; the default `all` keeps the previous selection unchanged. `active` selects records without a true `archived` field and `archived` only records with `archived: true`, in conjunction with the existing tag and path-text filters. Search still returns the complete stored records sorted by path without filling in a default field; export keeps the same document fields, five file statuses and `complete` rule.
14	
15	With reference expansion (`export --with-references`), the archive filter only chooses the starting documents: every referenced document is pulled in recursively regardless of its archive state, each path still appears once and cycles still terminate. For example, an active `policy.md` that references an archived `meeting.txt` still produces a manifest containing both under `--archive-state active --with-references`.
16	
17	Archiving only modifies the index; searching only reads stored metadata; exporting keeps its live file checks and never writes a manifest. Setting the archive state, or filtering with a state other than `all`, validates the whole index: invalid JSON or UTF-8, malformed record structures, references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths, and a non-boolean `archived` field all raise `ValueError`, even when the bad record is not selected. A non-string or unregistered path, a non-boolean `archived`, or a non-string/illegal `archive_state` also raises `ValueError`; index read/write failures raise `OSError`, and failed input validation never changes the index. With no index, setting the state is treated as an unregistered path and creates no file, while filtering returns an empty result (an empty manifest has `complete` false). The CLI prints JSON and exits 0 on success, or a JSON object containing `error` with exit code 2 on these failures.
18	
19	## Document categories
20	
21	`python3 document_room.py category policy.md --value "Legal Team"` assigns a single category to a registered document, and `DocumentRoom.set_category(relative_path, category)` does the same from Python; `--value` is required. The positional path matches the index's relative-path key exactly and case-sensitively, exactly as for `archive`: it is never resolved against the filesystem, the file is not parsed, and the category can be changed even when the original file has been deleted. The category must be a string; it is stripped of leading and trailing whitespace and stored as a `category` field, preserving case and any inner whitespace, and the updated full record is printed as JSON with exit 0. An empty (or all-whitespace) value stores `""` and marks the document uncategorized. Records written before this feature simply lack the field and are treated as uncategorized, without the field being added. Setting a category changes nothing else: other metadata, references and the archived state are preserved.
22	
23	The first `add` of a path never stores a `category` field; re-adding a path that already has one keeps its category along with its references and archived state. `search` and `export` (CLI flag `--category`, Python argument `category`) accept an optional category filter: omitting it or passing `None` keeps the previous selection unchanged, while an explicit empty string selects only uncategorized records. Both the stored category and the filter value are stripped of surrounding whitespace and then compared as full case-sensitive strings, in conjunction with the existing tag, path-text and archive filters. Search still returns the complete stored records sorted by path; export keeps the same document fields, five file statuses and `complete` rule, and the category filter only chooses the starting documents — with `--with-references` every referenced document is pulled in recursively regardless of its category, with the usual dedup, cycle termination and `complete` rules.
24	
25	Setting a category, or filtering with a category other than `None`, validates the whole index: invalid JSON or UTF-8, malformed record structures, references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths, a non-boolean `archived` field, and a stored `category` that is not a string all raise `ValueError`, even when the bad record is not selected. A non-string category, a non-string or unregistered path, or a filter value that is neither a string nor `None` also raises `ValueError`; index read/write failures raise `OSError`, and failed input validation never changes the index. With no index, setting a category is treated as an unregistered path and creates no file, while filtering returns an empty result. The CLI prints JSON and exits 0 on success, or a JSON object containing `error` with exit code 2 on these failures.
26	
27	## Version notes
28	
29	`python3 document_room.py note policy.md --value "v2 draft"` attaches a free-form version note to a registered document, and `DocumentRoom.set_version_note(relative_path, note)` does the same from Python; `--value` is required. The positional path matches the index's relative-path key exactly and case-sensitively, exactly as for `refs`: it is never resolved against the filesystem, the file is not parsed, and the note can be changed even when the original file has been deleted. The note must be a string; it is stripped of leading and trailing whitespace and stored as a `version_note` field, preserving case, inner whitespace and newlines, and the updated full record is printed as JSON with exit 0. An empty (or all-whitespace) value stores `""` and clears the note. Records written before this feature simply lack the field and are treated as having no note, without the field being added. Setting a note changes nothing else: other metadata, references, the archived state and the category are preserved.
30	
31	The first `add` of a path never stores a `version_note` field; re-adding a path that already has one keeps its note along with its references, archived state and category. `search` and `dump` return the stored note alongside the other metadata exactly as saved. `python3 document_room.py export --release "Q4 Launch" --with-version-notes` (or `export_manifest(..., include_version_notes=False)` with the flag on — the parameter is new, defaults to off, and the original parameter positions are unchanged) adds a `version_note` field to every manifest document: records without a stored note export `""`, and documents pulled in by reference expansion carry their own note. With the flag off no `version_note` field is added. Notes never participate in filtering, reference expansion, origin annotation, sorting, the five file statuses or the `complete` rule, and `compare` preserves the field in returned documents without comparing it.
32	
33	Setting a note, or exporting with notes enabled, validates the whole index: invalid JSON or UTF-8, malformed record structures or field types, references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths, and a stored `version_note` that is not a string all raise `ValueError`, even when the bad record is not selected. A non-string path or note, an unregistered path, or a non-boolean `include_version_notes` also raises `ValueError`; index read/write failures raise `OSError`, and failed input validation never changes the index. With no index, setting a note is treated as an unregistered path and creates no file, while a noted export returns an empty manifest with `complete` false. The CLI prints JSON and exits 0 on success, or a JSON object containing `error` with exit code 2 on these failures. Import keeps its existing conflict rules and extra-field preservation, and exporting never writes a manifest file or modifies the index or the original documents.
34	
35	## Release manifests
36	
37	`python3 document_room.py export --release "Q4 Launch" --tag legal --text policy` checks a release against the live files and prints `{"release", "complete", "documents"}`. The release name is required and trimmed; blank or non-string names raise `ValueError` from `DocumentRoom.export_manifest` (the CLI prints a JSON error and exits 2). `--tag` (repeatable, AND-combined) and `--text` (case-insensitive path substring) filter records with the same normalization as `search`. Documents are sorted by recorded relative path and keep their stored `path`, `name`, `bytes`, `sha256` and `tags`, plus a `status`:
38	
39	- `ready` — present, and both byte count and SHA-256 match the index;
40	- `changed` — present but the size or digest differs;
41	- `missing` — absent, a dangling symlink, or now a directory;
42	- `unsafe` — the resolved path escapes the document root (the target is never read);
43	- `unreadable` — any other resolution or read failure.
44	
45	Stored metadata is never overwritten with current values, and one document failing does not stop the others. `complete` is true only when the manifest is non-empty and every document is `ready`; an empty manifest still contains all three top-level fields. A missing index yields an empty manifest and is not created; malformed JSON or records whose structure/types do not match the registered format raise `ValueError`, and read failures raise `OSError`. Exporting only reads the index and files: it never copies documents, writes a manifest file or updates the index.
46	
47	## References
48	
49	`python3 document_room.py refs policy.md --to meeting.txt` records that a registered document directly refers to other registered documents, and `DocumentRoom.set_references(relative_path, targets)` does the same from Python. The source path is the positional argument and `--to` is repeatable; omitting `--to` clears the references. Paths match the index's relative-path keys exactly (case-sensitive) and are never resolved against the filesystem. Targets are deduplicated, sorted by path and stored as a `references` array on the record — an empty list is stored as `[]`. Self-references and mutual references are allowed. The updated record is returned as JSON and the CLI exits 0.
50	
51	A non-string source, an unregistered source or target, or targets that are not a list of strings raise `ValueError` without changing the index; a missing index is treated as empty and is not created. Corrupt JSON, records that do not match the registered format, a stored `references` field that is not a list of strings, or a stored reference to an unregistered path also raise `ValueError`, and index read/write failures raise `OSError`. Records written before this feature have no `references` field and are treated as having none: the first `add` of a path stores only the original fields, re-adding the same path keeps its references, and `search` returns any saved references alongside the other metadata.
52	
53	`python3 document_room.py export --release "Q4 Launch" --with-references` (or `export_manifest(..., include_references=True)`) expands the manifest: the usual tag and text filters pick the starting documents, then every referenced document is pulled in recursively — references are included whether or not they match the filters, each path appears once, and cycles still terminate. The manifest keeps the existing top-level and document fields sorted by path, every listed file is checked with the same status rules, and `complete` is false when any document is not `ready` or the manifest is empty. Reference-aware exports validate stored references as above; without the flag, export behaves exactly as before.
54	
55	## Reference origins
56	
57	`python3 document_room.py export --release "Q4 Launch" --with-references --with-origins` (or `export_manifest(..., include_references=True, include_origins=True)`) additionally records why each document entered the manifest. The option is off by default and requires reference expansion: a non-boolean `include_origins`, or enabling it without `include_references`, raises `ValueError`. Without the flag, export behaves exactly as before and no `origins` field is added.
58	
59	With origins enabled, every document gains an `origins` array whose entries are `{"path", "distance"}` objects: `path` is the registered path of a starting document (one selected by the tag, path-text, archive and category filters) and `distance` is the minimum number of reference edges from that starting document to this one, following the reference direction. Each reachable starting source appears at most once per document, a starting document lists itself with distance 0, shared documents keep every starting source, multiple routes collapse to the shortest distance, and self-references and cycles still terminate. `origins` is sorted by source path in case-sensitive lexicographic order, while `documents` keeps its usual path ordering. For example, with `a.md` and `b.md` selected, `a.md` referencing `c.md` directly and `b.md` reaching `c.md` through `d.md`, `c.md` lists `a.md` at distance 1 and `b.md` at distance 2 while `d.md` lists only `b.md`; if `c.md` also references `a.md`, then `a.md` additionally lists `b.md` at distance 3.
60	
61	Each document still appears once, an empty selection still yields an empty manifest with `complete` false, and the five file statuses and `complete` rule are unchanged. Enabling origins validates the whole index like reference expansion does — invalid JSON or UTF-8, malformed record structures or field types, and references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths raise `ValueError` even when the bad record is not selected, and index read failures raise `OSError`. Exporting remains read-only: it never writes a manifest file or updates the index, and a missing index is treated as empty without being created. `compare` preserves the `origins` field in returned documents like any other extra field and never compares it.
62	
63	## Reference impact
64	
65	`python3 document_room.py impact meeting.txt` answers the reverse question — which registered documents use a given document — and `DocumentRoom.reference_impact(target, transitive=False, include_routes=False)` does the same from Python. The positional path identifies the target with the same exact, case-sensitive relative-path key as `refs`; it is never resolved against the filesystem. By default only direct referrers are returned; pass `--transitive` (or `transitive=True`) to also include every document that reaches the target through one or more reference edges. The command prints `{"path", "documents"}` and exits 0, where `path` echoes the input key.
66	
67	Each document is the same record `search` returns plus an integer `distance`: the minimum number of reference edges from that document to the target. Direct referrers always have distance 1; transitive results add documents at greater distances. Results are sorted by distance ascending and then by relative path lexicographically, each path appears once, and the target itself is always excluded even when it references itself. Self-references and reference cycles stay legal and the query always terminates. A registered target that nobody references yields an empty `documents` array.
68	
69	Pass `--with-routes` (or `include_routes=True`) to also attach a `route` array to each document: one shortest reference chain explaining how that document depends on the target, starting at the referrer's own path and following registered references down to the target, so its length minus one equals `distance`. When several equally short chains exist, the one whose full path array is smallest in case-sensitive lexicographic order is shown, regardless of index or `references` ordering. Routes never repeat a path, and without the flag no `route` field is added; the result set, distances and ordering are unchanged either way.
70	
71	The impact query reads the stored index only: missing, changed or unreadable document files do not affect the result and no live file state is checked, and the index is never modified or created. A non-string or unregistered target, or a non-boolean `transitive` or `include_routes`, raises `ValueError`; a missing index is treated as empty (so any target is unregistered and no file is created). Corrupt JSON, records that do not match the registered format, a `references` field that is not a list of strings, or a reference to an unregistered path also raises `ValueError` — even when the offending record is unrelated to the target — and index read failures raise `OSError`. The CLI reports these as a JSON object with an `error` field and exit code 2. Old records without a `references` field are treated as having none, and the field is not added.
72	
73	## Duplicate registration query
74	
75	`python3 document_room.py duplicates --tag release --text docs` finds registered documents whose stored contents coincide, and `DocumentRoom.find_duplicates(tags=(), text="")` does the same from Python; both paths give identical results. `--tag` is repeatable and `--text` takes one value, both filtered with the same normalization as `search` (tags are trimmed, lowercased, empty tags ignored and combined with AND; text matches the relative path case-insensitively). With no filter every record is considered.
76	
77	Two records are duplicates only when both stored `bytes` and stored `sha256` are equal — the digest is compared as the exact stored string — and a group needs at least two distinct paths. `name`, `tags` and `references` never participate in the judgement, so same-named records with different contents are not grouped. The result is `{"groups": []}` when there are no duplicates or no group has a member the filter matches.
78	
79	Each group is `{"bytes", "sha256", "matched", "documents"}`: `matched` lists the paths of members that satisfy the filter, `documents` lists the group's full stored records from the whole index (with whatever fields were stored, including `references` when present; neither `references` nor `status` is added). Both arrays are sorted by path and contain each path once, and the groups themselves are sorted by the smallest member path. A filter hitting any single member returns the entire group: querying the `release` tag when only `a.txt` of two identical small files (`a.txt`, `b.txt`) carries it still returns both records, with `matched` listing just `a.txt`.
80	
81	The query reads the stored index only: modifying, deleting or replacing an original file with an escaping symlink does not change the result or the index, and a missing index yields empty groups without creating a file. The Python `tags` argument must be a list or tuple of strings and `text` a string, otherwise `ValueError` is raised. Invalid JSON or UTF-8, records not matching the registered format, a `references` field that is not a list of strings, or a reference to an unregistered path also raise `ValueError` — even when the offending record is not in a returned group — and index read failures raise `OSError`. The CLI prints JSON and exits 0 on success, or an object with an `error` field and exit code 2 on failure.
82	
83	## Metadata import
84	
85	`python3 document_room.py import --from records.json` merges a batch of registrations from another index into the current one, and `DocumentRoom.import_records(batch)` does the same from Python with the decoded dictionary; both paths give identical results. The source is a UTF-8 JSON object mapping each relative-path key to a complete record whose `path` equals the key — the same shape as the stored index. Importing only copies metadata: document files are never read or copied, so records register fine while their files are missing.
86	
87	Records are stored exactly as given: paths, tags and categories are not normalized, optional fields (`references`, `archived`, `category`) are not added, and any extra JSON fields are preserved. A successful import returns `{"added", "unchanged"}` — the paths this batch newly registered and the input paths that already existed with identical records — each sorted by path in case-sensitive lexicographic order, and the CLI prints it as JSON and exits 0.
88	
89	A path already registered counts as unchanged only when the existing and incoming records have exactly the same field set and values: array order matters, object key order does not, and a missing optional field differs from its explicit default. A same-path record with different data fails the whole batch with `ValueError` and nothing is overwritten. Both the batch and the merged index are validated against the registered format — required field types, `bytes` as a non-boolean integer, and the optional `references`, `archived` and `category` types — so a malformed record fails the import even when its path is not part of the batch. Every reference target must be registered in the union of the existing index and the batch; forward references within the batch, self-references and cycles are allowed, and an unregistered target fails the whole batch with `ValueError`.
90	
91	A non-object batch, invalid structure or field types, a key that does not match its record's `path`, and corrupt JSON or UTF-8 in the source file raise `ValueError`; reading the source file or the index and writing the index raise `OSError`. Any failure leaves the source file and the existing index untouched and registers nothing. A missing index is treated as empty; an empty batch or a batch whose records are all identical to the stored ones neither writes nor creates the index. After an import, `search` returns the full stored records and `export` keeps its five statuses, origin annotation and `complete` rule.
92	
93	## Metadata snapshot export
94	
95	`python3 document_room.py dump --tag legal --text policy` prints a metadata snapshot of the selected records as a JSON object mapping each relative-path key to its complete stored record — the same shape `import` accepts — and `DocumentRoom.export_records(tags=(), text="", archive_state="all", category=None)` does the same from Python; both paths give identical results. The command uses the global `--root` and `--index` options, prints only the JSON object with no wrapper and no file statuses, and exits 0. The snapshot can be saved and merged into another (empty) index with `import --from`.
96	
97	`--tag` (repeatable, AND-combined), `--text` (case-insensitive path substring), `--archive-state` and `--category` filter with the same semantics as `search`, and with no filter every record is a starting document. The filters only choose the starting documents: every referenced document is then pulled in recursively along the reference direction regardless of the filters — archived or deleted files included — each path appears once, and self-references and cycles terminate. Documents that merely reference a selected one are not included. Records are returned exactly as stored: extra JSON fields are preserved, array order, duplicate elements, case and whitespace are untouched, and missing optional fields are not filled in. The object is keyed by path in case-sensitive lexicographic order.
98	
99	The whole index is validated before the result is returned: invalid JSON or UTF-8, records that do not match the registered format, and references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths raise `ValueError` even when the bad record is not selected. A `tags` argument that is not a list or tuple of strings, a non-string `text`, an illegal `archive_state`, or a `category` that is neither a string nor `None` also raises `ValueError`; index read failures raise `OSError`. The CLI reports these as a JSON object with an `error` field and exit code 2, printing no partial snapshot. A missing index or an empty selection yields an empty object and creates no file. Dumping is read-only: it never reads or copies the original documents, never writes a snapshot file, and never modifies the index.
100	
101	## Registration removal
102	
103	`python3 document_room.py remove meeting.txt` unregisters a single document's metadata record, and `DocumentRoom.remove_record(relative_path, detach=False)` does the same from Python. The positional path matches the index's relative-path key exactly and case-sensitively, exactly as for `refs` and `archive`: it is never resolved against the filesystem, the document file is never read, moved or deleted, and removal works even when the original file has already been deleted. Only the index changes: no other registrations are recursively removed along reference edges.
104	
105	By default the operation is blocked with a `ValueError` whenever any *other* record's `references` contains the target path, and the index is left completely unchanged; the target's reference to itself never blocks its own removal. Records that merely reference one another transitively, without a direct edge to the target, do not block it. Pass `--detach` (or `detach=True`) to first remove every occurrence of the target from all other records' `references` and then remove the target's registration. Detaching preserves the order and any duplicate entries of the surviving references, never adds a `references` field to a record that lacked one, and stores `[]` on a record whose references all pointed at the target; every other field and every unaffected record keeps its stored value.
106	
107	A successful removal returns `{"removed", "updated"}`: `removed` is the target's complete record exactly as stored before the removal, and `updated` is an array of the complete records whose references were actually cleaned, sorted by path in case-sensitive lexicographic order — an empty array when nothing referenced the target (the default mode can only succeed in that case). The CLI prints the object as JSON and exits 0. After removal, `search`, `dump` and export operate on the remaining registrations; for example, once a referenced document is detached away, a reference-expanded listing only contains the surviving referrer.
108	
109	The whole index is validated against the same format `import` accepts before anything changes: a non-string or unregistered path, a non-boolean `detach`, corrupt JSON or UTF-8, malformed record structures or field types, and references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths all raise `ValueError` even when the offending record is unrelated to the target, and failed validation never writes the index. Index read/write failures raise `OSError`. A missing index is treated as an empty room: removing any path is reported as unregistered and no file is created. The CLI prints a JSON object containing `error` with exit code 2 on these failures.
110	
111	## Registration path migration
112	
113	`python3 document_room.py relocate meeting.txt docs/meeting.txt` moves a document's registration to a new path after you have moved the file yourself, keeping the original registration and every reference relationship, and `DocumentRoom.relocate_record(source, destination)` does the same from Python. The command uses the global `--root` and `--index` options and takes the old path first and the new path second. It only rewrites the stored index: document files are never moved, copied or deleted.
114	
115	The old path matches an index relative-path key exactly and case-sensitively, exactly as for `refs`, `archive` and `remove`: it is never resolved or read against the filesystem, so the migration works even when the original file has already been deleted. The new path follows the same resolution as `add` — joined under the document root, resolved, and stored as the canonical forward-slash relative path of the actual file (for example `docs/meeting.txt`, never with a `./` prefix). The target must exist and be a file inside the root; a target that resolves outside the root is rejected without being read, as are dangling links, symlink loops and paths that resolve outside the root. When either the target's byte count or its SHA-256 differs from the original registration, `ValueError` is raised and the content metadata is not refreshed; bytes, digest, tags and every other stored field keep their registered values rather than being updated from the new file.
116	
117	On success the old index key is replaced by the new canonical key. The moved record's `path` becomes the canonical new path and its `name` the target file's name; `bytes`, `sha256`, `tags` and every other field keep their values, and optional fields that were absent stay absent. Every `references` array in the index that contains the old key is rewritten to use the new key, including the moved record's own self-reference. Rewriting preserves array order and duplicate entries, never adds a `references` field to a record that lacked one, and self-references and reference cycles stay legal. For example, with `policy.md` referencing `meeting.txt`, moving the latter to `docs/meeting.txt` makes both the stored reference and the reference-expanded manifest listing use the new key.
118	
119	The result is `{"before", "after", "updated"}`: `before` is the moved record's complete record as stored before the migration (with the old path and name), `after` is its complete record after the migration, and `updated` lists only the *other* complete records whose references were actually replaced, sorted by path in case-sensitive lexicographic order — an empty array when nothing else referenced the old key. The CLI prints the object as JSON and exits 0.
120	
121	After a migration, `search`, `dump`, `impact`, `duplicates`, reference expansion, origin annotation and manifest export all use the new key; existing entry points, tag/text/archive/category filter semantics, the five file statuses and the `complete` rule are unchanged.
122	
123	The whole index is validated against the same format `import` accepts before anything changes — record structure, the public optional field types (`references`, `archived`, `category`, `version_note`) and every reference target — so corrupt JSON or UTF-8, malformed records or field types, and dangling references all raise `ValueError` even when the bad record is unrelated to the migration; any failed validation leaves the index bytes exactly as they were. A non-string source or destination, an unregistered old key, a destination canonical key that is already registered (including when it equals the old key), a missing or non-file target, a target resolving outside the root, or a symlink loop also raises `ValueError`. File or index read/write failures raise `OSError`. A missing index is treated as an unregistered old key and creates no file. The CLI prints a JSON object containing `error` with exit code 2 on these failures.
124	
125	## Batch tag editing
126	
127	`python3 document_room.py tags policy.md meeting.txt --add legal --add release --remove draft` edits the stored tags of one or more registered documents in a single batch, and `DocumentRoom.edit_tags(paths, add_tags=(), remove_tags=())` does the same from Python; all three parameters accept only a list or tuple of strings. The command uses the global `--root` and `--index` options and takes one or more positional paths, with repeatable `--add` and `--remove` flags (each may be omitted). Paths match the index's relative-path keys exactly and case-sensitively, exactly as for `refs` and `archive`: they are never resolved against the filesystem, duplicate paths are processed only once, and editing works even when the original files have been deleted, changed or made unreadable — document files are never read or modified.
128	
129	Both the input tags and each selected record's existing tags use `add`'s normalization: surrounding whitespace is trimmed, letters are lowercased, and empty items are ignored. The resulting tag set is the normalized existing set with `remove_tags` taken out and `add_tags` added, deduplicated and saved in lexicographic order. Adding a tag the record already has and removing a tag it never had are both allowed. If the normalized add and remove sets overlap, `ValueError` is raised and nothing changes. A record counts as updated whenever the stored tags array differs from the result, including changes caused by normalization alone (case, whitespace, duplicates or ordering); otherwise the path is listed as unchanged and its record is not rewritten.
130	
131	The result is `{"updated", "unchanged"}`: `updated` is an array of the complete updated records and `unchanged` an array of paths, both sorted by path in case-sensitive lexicographic order with each path appearing once. An empty `paths` list returns two empty arrays. Only the selected records' `tags` arrays change: every other field (and the absence of an optional field) is preserved exactly as stored, unselected records are byte-for-byte untouched, and when every selected record is unchanged the index is not written at all. The CLI prints the result as JSON and exits 0.
132	
133	The whole index is validated against the same format `import` accepts before anything changes: invalid JSON or UTF-8, malformed record structures or public field types (`references`, `archived`, `category`, `version_note`), references that are not lists of strings or point at unregistered paths all raise `ValueError`, even when the bad record is not selected. Parameters with the wrong container or member type, or any path that is not registered (including a case mismatch), also raise `ValueError`; failed validation never writes the index. A missing index is treated as an empty room: non-empty paths fail without creating the file, while an empty path list returns the empty result without creating it. Index read/write failures raise `OSError`. The CLI prints a JSON object containing `error` with exit code 2 on these failures and also when no paths are given.
134	
135	After an edit, the existing entry points use the new values: `search`, `dump`, `duplicates`, `impact`, reference expansion, origin annotation and manifest export all read the edited tags. `add` keeps its refresh behavior (re-adding a file recomputes bytes, SHA-256 and tags from the file), reference relationships, duplicate grouping, the manifest statuses and `complete` rule, and every other entry point's semantics are unchanged.
136	
137	## Manifest comparison
138	
139	`python3 document_room.py compare --before old.json --after new.json` diffs two manifests previously produced by `export` (plain UTF-8 JSON files), and `DocumentRoom.compare_manifests(before, after)` does the same from Python with the manifest dictionaries; both paths give identical results. The comparison relies solely on the manifest snapshots: the inputs and index are never modified, no document files are read, and nothing is created. The two manifests may use the same release name or different filter selections.
140	
141	The result is `{"before", "after", "added", "removed", "changed", "unchanged"}`. `before` and `after` echo each input's `release` and `complete` (release/complete differences never affect document classification and `complete` is never recomputed). `added` lists complete documents present only in the second manifest and `removed` those present only in the first; `changed` lists `{"path", "before", "after", "fields"}` keeping both full documents plus the changed field names; `unchanged` lists paths with no compared change.
142	
143	Documents pair by case-sensitive exact `path` (no normalization); only `name`, `bytes`, `sha256`, `tags` and `status` are compared. Tags compare as string sets, ignoring order and duplicates (but not case or whitespace); the other fields compare by value, so a `status`-only change still counts as changed. Extra document fields are preserved in the returned documents but never compared. Each category is sorted by path and `fields` is sorted by field name; each path appears exactly once. Two empty manifests yield four empty categories.
144	
145	Each input must be an object with a non-blank string `release`, a boolean `complete` and an array `documents`; every document needs string `path`, `name` and `sha256`, a non-boolean integer `bytes`, an array of strings `tags`, and one of the five statuses, with no duplicate paths within a manifest. Extra fields are allowed. Bad structure or types, duplicate paths, invalid statuses, and JSON or UTF-8 decode errors raise `ValueError` (the CLI prints a JSON error and exits 2); unreadable files raise `OSError`.
146	
147	Run `python3 -B -m unittest -v` for the API, path-boundary and CLI tests.
148
